newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Duke poised as generating powerhouse.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Duke poised as generating powerhouse.

text.p: With its $7.7 billion merger with PanEnergy Corp, Duke Power Co positioned itself as a powerhouse in the soon-to-be deregulated domestic and rapidly expanding international electric generating industries, company executives said on Monday.

The stock transaction also solidified the standing of the merged company -- to be renamed Duke Energy Corp -- in the top tier of U.S. electric and natural gas wholesalers, company executives said on Monday.

"We think we have a competitive advantage in power generation," Duke Chairman William Grigg said. "We would see this combination as affording us a way to more aggressively expand that power generation business."

Charlotte, N.C.-based Duke and Houston's PanEnergy unveiled plans to merge their respective electric and natural gas businesses into a $23 billion conglomerate, the latest merger in a rapidly consolidating domestic energy industry.
Company executives said talks on the merger began in late-July, just days after Enron Corp announced its $3.2 billion acquisition of Portland General Corp.

That deal, which combines the trading expertise of a natural gas company with the operating know-how of a leading electric utility, is considered a blueprint for creation of a nationwide electric and gas retailer.

With retail competition expected in some states as soon as January 1998, Duke executives hinted they will focus on consoldating electric generating capacity to compete in the emerging nationwide energy marketplace.
"We don't see the need for any greenfield power generation, but we do think there will be opportunities to acquire additional generating assets," Grigg said.
In addition to expanding its wholesale energy trading operations, the merger gives Duke access to a source of fuel for current and future gas-fired electric plants.

"Gas is clearly the fuel of choice for new generation going forward, and it makes sense that if gas is the fuel of choice -- which means it will control the price of electricity -- it makes sense for Duke to have control over supply," Grigg said.

Both companies had joint energy marketing ventures in place -- Duke with its Duke-Louis Dreyfus venture and PanEnergy's venture with Mobil Corp -- and executives said those ventures would remain in place.

"The folding together of those two joint ventures leaves us in the top two or three gas marketers in the market today and the top two or three electric marketers in the market today," Duke President Richard Priory said.
Limited regulatory approvals are needed to close the deal, and executives see the merger closing in less than 12 months.

Duke currently serves 1.8 million electric customers in North and South Carolina. PanEnergy operates 37,000 miles of natural gas pipelines, handling 15 percent of the natural gas comsumed domestically.
